te: Report on managing migrant workers, a case study of Ranong Province
se: The meeting considered the study report on approaches to managing migrant workers, a case study of Ranong Province, with proposals such as setting up an agency dedicated to migrant workers, creating a national labour development digital platform, bringing in workers through the MOU system, adapting laws to each area, and developing language skills. It also considered a petition about recruitment by an agency and a request to disclose meeting records on the rules for electing the Social Security Board
it: Petition: request for fair treatment in the application and hiring process of an agency
Request to disclose to the public the meeting records on amending the rules for electing the Social Security Board
Study report: approaches to managing migrant workers, a case study of Ranong Province (challenges, policy, and economic and social effects)

te: Findings on e-Work Permits, employment of persons with disabilities, and government service contracts summarised
se: The meeting considered a petition on the effects of government agencies' service contracts that may not be in line with the procurement law (assigning the Subcommittee on Labour Welfare to gather information), noted the summary of information gathered on e-Work Permits, with proposals to extend the deadlines for applications, documents and fees and for the Department of Employment to examine the complaints, and noted the summary on protecting the employment rights of persons with disabilities under sections 33 and 35
it: Petition: effects of government agencies' service contracts that may not be in line with the Public Procurement Act
Summary of the petition on the Department of Employment's e-Work Permit project: deadlines to be extended, short- and long-term fixes proposed, and the complaints to be examined
Summary of the petition on protecting the employment rights of persons with disabilities under sections 33 and 35

te: Independent and platform workers, and observations on restructuring the Social Security Office
se: The meeting followed up the subcommittees' work: a study of approaches to protecting independent and platform workers, and the restructuring of the Social Security Office, on which the subcommittee heard the agencies concerned and made observations, such as that laws and regulations must be consistent, and on the qualifications of executives under the new structure. It also considered a complaint that someone had claimed a position on a subcommittee
it: Subcommittees: approaches to solving problems in protecting independent and platform workers
Restructuring the Social Security Office (hearing the Social Security Office, the Fiscal Policy Office and other agencies)
Complaint that someone had claimed a position on a subcommittee

te: Petitioners heard on government service contracts and on the project to outsource e-Work Permit services
se: The meeting heard information on a petition asking for a circular on government service contracts to be withdrawn, and on a petition concerning the Department of Employment's project to hire a private company to produce work permits and receive applications from foreign nationals (Outsourcing Service or e-Work Permit), assigning the subcommittee to gather information before reporting to the committee. It noted the subcommittees' work and appointed advisers and a working group to study the law on employing older persons
it: Petition: circular on contracts for government service contract staff
Petition: the Department of Employment's project to hire a private company to produce work permits and receive applications from foreign nationals (e-Work Permit)
Following up the work of all 3 subcommittees (Employment Services and Skills Development · Labour Welfare and Protection · Social Security)
3 honorary advisers to the committee appointed
A working group set up to study the law on employing older persons and post-retirement workers (4 more members), and 5 subcommittee advisers appointed

te: Petitions on government service contracts and on provident fund compensation
se: The meeting considered a petition asking the Comptroller General's Department to withdraw a circular on approaches to revising contracts for government service contract staff, and a petition from employees of the Port Authority of Thailand concerning compensation in the provident fund system under a 2014 resolution of the PAT board. It resolved to invite the petitioners and agencies concerned to give information on 30 March 2026, approved the subcommittees' work reports, and appointed 1 honorary advisers
it: Petition: request for the Comptroller General's Department to withdraw a circular on contracts for government service contract staff
Petition: compensation in the provident fund system under the 2014 resolution of the Port Authority of Thailand board
Following up the work of all 3 subcommittees (Employment Services and Skills Development · Labour Welfare and Protection · Social Security)
1 honorary advisers to the committee appointed

te: Help for Thai workers in the Middle East, and delays in the e-Work Permit system
se: The meeting considered approaches to helping Thai workers affected by the unrest in the Middle East, and invited the petitioners and the Department of Employment to give information on difficulties and delays in applying for work permits and notifying employment in the e-Work Permit system
it: Approaches to helping Thai workers affected by the unrest in the Middle East
Petition: difficulties and delays in applying for work permits and notifying employment in the e-Work Permit system (the Department of Employment invited to give information)

te: Employment rights of persons with disabilities, direct election of the Social Security Board, and the Samut Sakhon report (revised)
se: The meeting invited the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities to give information on a petition about the employment of persons with disabilities under sections 33 and 35, noted the subcommittee's preliminary information on a labour network's request to keep direct elections of the Social Security Board (1 person, 1 vote), and considered the revised draft study report on migrant workers, a case study of Samut Sakhon Province
it: Petition: protecting the rights of persons with disabilities in employment under sections 33 and 35 (the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities invited to give information)
Preliminary information gathered: proposal to keep direct elections of the Social Security Board, 1 person, 1 vote
Draft study report on irregular migrant workers and occupations prohibited to foreign nationals, a case study of Samut Sakhon Province (revised)

te: Employment rights of persons with disabilities, problems booking work permit renewals, and the report on migrant workers in Samut Sakhon
se: The meeting considered a petition asking for protection of the employment rights of persons with disabilities under sections 33 and 35, and a petition that queue bookings with the outside service provider in the e-Work Permit system could not be made. It considered the draft study report on the motion on irregular migrant workers and occupations reserved for Thais (a case study of Samut Sakhon Province), and followed up the subcommittees' work, such as employing older persons and a draft law to promote and protect independent workers

Petition: appointments to renew migrant workers' work permits cannot be booked in the e-Work Permit system
Draft study report on the motion: irregular migrant workers and occupations prohibited to foreign nationals, a case study of Samut Sakhon Province
Subcommittees: skills development and promoting employment of older persons · effects of the draft Independent Workers Promotion and Protection Act B.E. ....

te: Foreign nationals running trading businesses, a study visit to Trang prepared, and positions in a subcommittee adjusted
se: The meeting noted a petition, referred from a local project, about the problem of foreign nationals running trading businesses unlawfully (as alleged), noted the schedule of a study visit and seminar in Trang Province, followed up the subcommittees' work, and approved changes of positions and the appointment of advisers in a subcommittee
it: Petition: the problem of foreign nationals running trading businesses unlawfully (as alleged)

te: Criteria for appointing advisers and working groups set, the report of the visit to Japan received, and a study visit to Trang prepared
se: The meeting approved criteria for appointing honorary advisers, subcommittee advisers and working groups (who must have knowledge or experience in the committee's work), approved in principle the report of the trip for a bilateral meeting in Japan on 9–14 November 2025, and approved the study visit and seminar in Trang Province on 16–18 February 2026

te: Work begins for 2026: a labour dispute at an auto parts factory, subcommittee plans, and changes of positions in the committee
se: At the first meeting of 2026 (12 January 2026), the meeting followed a labour dispute at an auto parts manufacturer that may affect employees and assigned the Subcommittee on Labour Welfare and Protection to gather information from all sides. It noted the subcommittees' results for 2025 and plans for 2026 (migrant workers, a digital labour platform and work by older persons), and approved filling vacant positions in the committee
it: Labour dispute between a labour union and an auto parts manufacturer that may lead to a lockout
Results for 2025 and plans for 2026 of the Subcommittee on Employment Services: migrant workers, a digital labour platform, future industries, and work by older persons
Subcommittee on Social Security: the new old-age pension formula (CARE formula) for insured persons under sections 33 and 39
Vacant positions in the committee filled: Mr. Chinnachot Saengsank, First Vice-Chair · Mrs. Ajala Na Ranong, Third Vice-Chair · Mrs. Nongluk Kankhiao, Secretary

te: Petition on human trafficking for labour: the screening committee has found 42 of 44 people to be victims, and an AI study topic set for 2027
se: The meeting gathered preliminary facts on a petition seeking fairness in a case of victims of human trafficking for forced labour or services, inviting the petitioners and the Director-General of the Department of Employment. The petitioners say they have suffered because they have not yet been recognised as victims of human trafficking, after being deceived into working in Cambodia, held against their will, and having their personal bank accounts used as mule accounts, so they have had to give statements in several provinces. Information from the Ministry of Labour states that the screening committee (the Department of Special Investigation, the Ministry of Social Development and Human Security and the Ministry of Labour) had found 13 of 44 people to be victims because the evidence was not yet sufficient; after more evidence was gathered on 13 November 2026, 42 people in total have been found to be victims, evidence for the other 2 is still being gathered, and the documents will be processed once all 44 are complete. The subcommittee will send what it has gathered to the Committee on Labour, recommending that the matter be sent to the Senate Committee on Laws and Justice and that the petitioners be informed. The meeting also set its study plan for 2027 on the effects of artificial intelligence on workers. The next meeting is on Wednesday 2 December 2026 at 13.30
it: Preliminary facts gathered on a petition seeking fairness in a case of victims of human trafficking for forced labour or services (petitioners and the Director-General of the Department of Employment invited)

Study plan for 2027: the effects of applying artificial intelligence technology (Generative AI) on the career sustainability of entry-level and mid-level workers in Thailand (an estimated 2.2 million Thai workers are at risk of being replaced, and demand for AI skills has risen 3.9 times)

te: Pre-meeting video · Petition on human trafficking for labour: the screening committee has found 42 of 44 people to be victims, and an AI study topic set for 2027
Proposals on urban employment and community careers for older people
se: The meeting received a further report from the working group studying the law on employing older persons and post-retirement workers on health, income and suitable work for older people. According to 2024 data, Thailand has about 14 million people aged 60 and over, or 20% of the population, of whom about 5.3 million are working. The working group proposed assessing readiness according to the actual nature of the work, adjusting workloads and rest periods, and piloting a job-matching service for older people through district offices or municipalities
it: Proposals to promote urban employment and community careers for older people

te: Meeting summary video · Proposals on urban employment and community careers for older people
Proposed system for employment and career development of older people, 2027–2047
se: The meeting followed up the progress of the working group studying the law on employing older persons and post-retirement workers on employment, career promotion and group enterprises for older people in communities. The working group presented a proposed long-term system for the employment and career development of older people, based on letting older people choose work voluntarily and according to their health, and addressing scattered data, inflexible work and the lack of mechanisms linking local markets
it: Proposed system for employment and career development of older people in Thailand, 2027–2047
